title: Deployment cocoon checklist and canary sampling playbook — 2026-07 (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a low-risk, phased rollout pattern Im calling the 'deployment cocoon'. The idea: wrap a feature rollout in progressively looser safety layers (cocoon) while collecting targeted telemetry sampling so we can reason about regression risk and customer impact before broad exposure.

Audience: release engineers, on-call operators, SREs, and solutions engineers responsible for Dedicated/Private rollouts.

Summary (one-liner):
- Start small with strict routing + heavy telemetry sampling; expand channels as passive quality signals remain green; maintain fast rollback/flip triggers and a clear handoff script for the 24h steady-state.

High-level constraints:
- Target platform: Redwood Dedicated + Hosted fallback.
- SLA sensitivity: medium-high (latency budget matters).
- Canary window: minimum 90 minutes, recommended 6 hours per traffic tier during initial rollout.

Cocoon principle (operational steps):
1) Isolate: route 0.1-1% traffic to a dedicated canary pool pinned to the new variant.
2) Inspect: apply fine-grained telemetry sampling (100% traces for errors; 10% for successful requests; prefix/kv-cache hit metrics).
3) Harden: if green, expand to 5-10% with relaxed but still guarded policies (autoscale cap, token-rate caps).
4) Share: after 24–48h of stable metrics, onboard regional/enterprise routes with slow ramping.
5) Release: open general availability only after stability and quality thresholds satisfied.

Canary sampling heuristics (recipes):
- Error tracing: sample 100% of requests where status != 200, or token-generation aborted. Send full stack + input substring (first 256 chars).
- Successful sampling: 10% uniform, but bias to long-lived sessions and high-cost tokens (>512 tokens) at 30% to catch perf regressions.
- KV cache heatmap: log prefix cache hit/miss at request-level (aggregate to per-minute). Sampleing rate 20%.
- Semantic quality checks: run a small auto-eval prompt-set (10 prompts) against canary model every 30m; log per-prompt divergence vs baseline.
- Cost telemetry: record per-request token compute-time (ms/token) and estimated $/1000 tokens.

Quick 7-day rollout calendar (example window for a non-blocking feature):
- Day 0 (preflight): branch build -> integration smoke. Merge blocked until preflight OK. Ops: handshake channel opened (#deploy-cocoon).
- Day 0, +2h: spin canary pool (pinned nodes x1). Fire canary tests: lint, smoke, small eval set.
- Day 0, +2–4h: route 0.25% traffic. Observe p50/p95 latency, error rate, mem/gpu.
- Day 0, +6h: if green, expand to 1%. Run extended semantic eval and cross-region latency checks.
- Day 1: after 24h green metrics, increase to 5% and apply autoscale cap removal in one-region.
- Day 2–3: 10% across regions; run customer-sample probes for any high-SLA accounts (pre-notify customers flagged in list).
- Day 4–7: gradual expansion to 50% with daily stability gates; by Day 7 consider GA release or move to long-tail verification for 48–72h.

Preflight checklist (must pass before canary):
- Build artifacts: hash, signed, and stored in artifact repo (sha512).
- Smoke tests: end-to-end smoke on staging with synthetic traffic (30s burst).
- Migration plan: if any model/weights changes, verify artifacts in S3 and compatibility matrix.
- Observability hooks: dashboards created + alert rules staged (links below).
- Rollback artifact: verified previous good binary available and tested for quick re-deploy (rollback runbook updated).
- Communication: stakeholders notified (GTM, CS owners for impacted customers).

Canary watch checklist (first 6 hours):
- Metrics to watch: error-rate (5xx), p95 latency, sustained GPU utilization, token-per-second throughput, cache-hit ratio.
- Thresholds (hard triggers): error-rate > 0.5% over 5m OR p95 latency increase > 30% over baseline OR token/ms/token > 2x baseline => immediate rollback.
- Soft triggers (alert + investigate): memory growth trends, tail-latency uplift > 15%, semantic divergence score > 0.1 average.
- Actions on soft trigger: pause expansion, re-run eval-set, collect full traces for last 30m, convene on-call + release lead.

Operator handoff script (30-min window, TL;DR):
- On-call opens #deploy-cocoon.
- Confirm canary pool health: 3/3 node readiness and no GPU OOMs.
- Check dashboard (p50/p95, errors by API key, by region).
- If rollback required: run rollback script (deploy rollback artifact ID), re-route traffic back to previous variant, confirm warmup, post-rollback postmortem stub created.

Release notes draft (to include in public-facing release brief):
- Feature: incremental model routing and autoscaling refinements to reduce cold-start latency by X–Y% (internal benchmark).
- Impact: predictable improve latency on long-context batches; no expected change to response semantics.
- Opt-in: new routing occurs only for select traffic lanes during canary; no change to customer SDK surface.
- Known limitations: small class of <2% high-token requests observed with slight memory churn (monitoring enabled).

Smoke test matrix (examples):
- Endpoint: /v1/generate -> tests: short prompt, long prompt (1k tokens), streaming path.
- Endpoint: embeddings -> tests: batch size 16, concurrency 10.
- Edge case: truncated KV cache checkpoint recovery after warm restart.

Rollback and remediation playbook (short):
1) Stop routing to canary pool.
2) Deploy rollback artifact to canary nodes and gradually shift traffic back to known-good pool.
3) If rollback fails (new artifact has broader issue), engage SRE-runbook-rollback-rapid (page on-call infra lead).
4) Postmortem owner assigned within 24h.

Open questions / unresolved risks:
- How to include Dedicated customers that have pinned models but expect instant pin-to-GA? (Need process decision: opt-in sandbox or notify and schedule controlled expansion).
- Does our billing/chargeback logic correctly handle partial canary traffic billing (fractional accounting)? Finance check requested (JIRA-FIN-88).
- Sampling privacy: semantic sample excerpts contain user content; confirm retention & PII strip policy for canary traces. Security review queued (SEC-192).

Next steps / TODOs:
- Marcus: implement 10-minute rolling-eval hook in canary cluster (ETA 2026-07-08).
- Diego: add alert thresholds to the p95-latency dashboard + adjust anomaly detector window (ETA 2026-07-06).
- Lena: draft customer-facing note for flagged enterprise accounts and schedule a 1:1 if impact detected (ETA 2026-07-07).
- Me (Aisha): iterate on rollback script to include snapshot restore of KV cache for canary nodes.

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratch):
- Consider a "cocoon mode" feature flag in infra that auto-enables heavy sampling + conservative autoscaling caps; make it a single toggle for future rollouts.
- Low-effort QA: add a small synthetic customer workload that mimics enterprise traffic every 8h.

Appendix (links & quick commands):
- Canary deploy script: runtime/tools/deploy_cocoon.sh --cluster canary1 --artifact <id>
- Dashboards: /dash/telemetry/cocoon-canary | /dash/semantics/canary-eval
- Quick rollback: runtime/ops/rollback.sh --artifact <good-id> --confirm

Status: draft. This doc is intended to converge into a canonical runbook after 2 successful cocoon rollouts.
